title: Functions Continued
objectives: Pass data to functions using parameters
Use default parameters for optional values
Design pure functions following best practices
description: Master advanced function concepts including parameters, return values, scope, and default parameters. Learn to design professional functions. Build temperature converters and discount calculators!

exercises.title: Neural Sync: Function with Parameter
exercises.description: Define a function that takes a parameter.

exercises.title: Neural Sync: Return Statement
exercises.description: Define a function that returns a value.
exercises.targetCode:
def add(a, b):
    return a + b

exercises.title: Neural Sync: Default Parameter
exercises.description: Define a function with a default parameter.
exercises.targetCode:
def power(base, exp=2):
    return base ** exp

exercises.title: Glitch Fix: Missing Argument
exercises.description: Function expects 2 arguments but only gets 1! Add the second argument.
exercises.brokenCode:
def multiply(x, y):
    return x * y
result = multiply(5)
print(result)

exercises.title: Glitch Fix: No Return
exercises.description: Function calculates but doesn't return the result! Add return statement.
exercises.brokenCode:
def square(n):
    result = n * n
x = square(5)
print(x)

exercises.title: Field Mission: Temperature Converter
exercises.description: Create celsius_to_fahrenheit(c) that returns F = C * 9/5 + 32. Test with 0.

exercises.title: Field Mission: Circle Area
exercises.description: Create circle_area(radius) that returns π * r² (use 3.14159). Test with radius 5.

exercises.title: Field Mission: Max Finder
exercises.description: Create max_of_two(a, b) that returns the larger number. Test with 15 and 23.

exercises.title: Neural Sync: Coordinates Function
exercises.description: Function with 2 parameters returning formatted coordinates.
exercises.targetCode:
def format_coords(lat, lon):
    return f'({lat}, {lon})'

result = format_coords(40.7, -74.0)
print(result)

exercises.title: Neural Sync: Multi-Parameter Combat Calculator
exercises.description: Professional damage calculator with 3 parameters and complex logic.
exercises.targetCode:
# Combat damage calculator
def calculate_damage(base_dmg, multiplier, armor):
    total = base_dmg * multiplier - armor
    return total

damage = calculate_damage(50, 2, 10)
print('Damage dealt:', damage)

exercises.title: Debug Challenge: Parameter Mismatch
exercises.description: Function expects 2 params but only 1 provided! Pass both arguments!
exercises.brokenCode:
def add(a, b):
    return a + b

result = add(5)
print(result)
exercises.starterCode:
def add(a, b):
    return a + b

result = add(5)
print(result)
exercises.solution:
def add(a, b):
    return a + b

result = add(5, 10)
print(result)

exercises.title: Crypto Math: XOR Cipher
exercises.description: Create xor_cipher(value, key) that returns value ^ key. Test with (42, 7).
exercises.solution:
def xor_cipher(value, key):
    return value ^ key

result = xor_cipher(42, 7)
print(result)

exercises.title: Field Logic: Threat Assessor
exercises.description: Function assess_threat(enemies, agents) returns True if enemies > agents, else False. Test (30, 20).
exercises.solution:
def assess_threat(enemies, agents):
    return enemies > agents

result = assess_threat(30, 20)
print(result)

exercises.title: Resource Manager: Supply Calculator
exercises.description: Function calc_supplies(days, per_day) returns days*per_day. Call with (7, 3) and print.
exercises.solution:
def calc_supplies(days, per_day):
    return days * per_day

total = calc_supplies(7, 3)
print(total)

exercises.title: Boss Challenge: Mission Success Probability
exercises.description: Function success_rate(skill, difficulty, equipment). score = skill + equipment - difficulty. If score > 50 return 'HIGH', elif > 20 return 'MEDIUM', else 'LOW'. Test (60, 30, 25).
